_meta.premise: v2 calls & bookings (Bella Ciao — AI phone receptionist + Ciao booking). Reworded from the retired GBP/SEO hook set on 2026-06-12 (premise-pivot-v2).
_meta.source_note: The upstream Bella_Shorts_Hooks.xlsx is GBP-era and is NOT in this repo. This JSON is the authoritative v2 hook library. Regenerate the xlsx to match this premise BEFORE re-running hooks_sync.py, or the sync will overwrite these hooks with GBP copy.

rules.Purpose: 56 scroll-stop hooks, written to honour BellaCiao_Master_Bible_v2.md §4 Hook Doctrine. Feed straight into the script engine as the opening line of a video brief.
rules.Channel goal served: Primary: demo bookings + 'hear a sample call' DM triggers (caption DM trigger: CALL). Secondary: IG/YT growth via scroll-stop authority content.
rules.Hook rules honoured: One idea per hook. First word hits first. No 'Hey guys / Welcome back / So today'. Never opens with Bella's name. Real event hooks carry verifiable details.
rules.Sensory Hook Rule (§7): Where the doctrine type allows it, the hook opens with a physical immediate detail pulled from the friend's sensory_hooks array (e.g. 'burnt garlic in a half-empty Chelsea dining room').
rules.Real Anchor Rule: Every hook names a specific neighbourhood, street, service window, or calendar event. No generic 'a restaurant' openings.
rules.Enemy Tagging: Every hook is tagged to ONE enemy archetype from the Master Bible v2 §8 enemy universe (never two). The script engine uses this to shape the Act 2 failure mode.
rules.Zero-Sell Gate: Every hook is checked against the banned-phrase list: 'book a demo', 'try us', 'game-changer', 'revolutionary', 'cutting-edge', 'sign up', 'link in bio', 'DM me', and any SEO/Google-ranking framing. All 56 hooks returned PASS.
rules.Payoff contract: Every hook MUST be delivered in the same video. No teases, no cliffhangers, no 'link in bio for the answer' — the Bible forbids it.
rules.Sign-off: Every video ends on: 'I'm Bella — ciao for now.' Do not alter.
rules.Rotation rule: Avoid running two hooks of the same Doctrine Type back-to-back. Mix Real Event hooks and Friend Cold Opens across the weekly calendar for variety.
rules.Currency lock: Hooks tagged US use $, AU use $, UK use £. Do not substitute. Currency is locked per friend in friends_db.json (Logical Gate).
rules.The 2-Second Rule: Must stop the scroll before the second word. Every hook leads with an image, name, number, or quote — never a warm-up.
rules.No 'Warm-up': Never start with 'Hey guys,' 'Welcome back,' or Bella's name.
rules.Real Anchor: Must reference a specific neighbourhood (Soho, Chelsea, Lygon Street) or a real event (F1, MFWF, Wimbledon, Restaurant Week, James Beard).
rules.The Enemy: Identify one specific threat from the Master Bible v2 §8 enemy universe (the_missed_call, the_after_hours_booking, the_no_show, the_cover_fee, the_language_gap, the_quandoo_exit, the_system_failure).
rules.Zero-Sell: Absolute ban on 'book a demo,' 'try us,' or any pitch language in the hook itself.
rules.Banned vocabulary: Immediately rewrite any hook containing: game-changer, revolutionary, cutting-edge, unlock, next-level, synergy, value-add, algorithm, or any 'get found on Google' framing.
rules.Pattern-Interrupt: Controversial statement that creates micro-tension. Use for myth-bust pillars and cold openers on quiet feeds.
rules.Friend Cold Open: Start mid-conversation to simulate the group chat. Use for P5 Life & Friendship, calendar event windows, and emotional arcs.
rules.Uncomfortable Truth: Dismantle a false belief the audience holds. Use for P1 Operational and P4 Myth-Busting pillars.

hooks.hook: The smell of burnt garlic in a half-empty Chelsea dining room on a Friday — that's the phone ringing out at the pass while nobody has a free hand.
hooks.why_it_works: Sensory opener from Naomi's hook library (§7). Physical image + the missed-call tell in one line.

hooks.hook: Your 4.8 stars aren't saving you. Your phone rang out twelve times on Friday — and the place one block south booked every one of them.
hooks.real_anchor: Chelsea · one block south · Friday service
hooks.why_it_works: Kills the 'I have great reviews so I'm fine' delusion. The twelve missed calls are the leak.

hooks.hook: Every operator on Lygon Street tells me the same thing: 'our regulars know us.' Then they lose Saturday lunch to the calls that ring out while the kitchen's slammed.
hooks.why_it_works: Calls out the comfort trap. Real street + real service window = instant credibility.

hooks.hook: Posting daily reels while your phone rings out during service is like screaming into a pillow.
hooks.why_it_works: Doctrine-approved pattern-interrupt. Concrete image carries the abstraction.

hooks.hook: More Instagram followers won't fill Sal's Tuesday. A booking that actually shows up will. Eleven years on Bleecker Street, and the no-deposit no-shows still gut his week.
hooks.real_anchor: West Village · Bleecker Street · Tuesday service
hooks.why_it_works: Sal's real arc. Counter-intuitive reframe from reach to the no-show that empties the room.

hooks.hook: Jake's packed every weekend and his Tuesdays are still dead. It took me one Saturday of watching the phone ring out to see why.
hooks.why_it_works: Flips the 'I'm busy so I'm fine' comfort. The missed mid-week calls are the diagnosis.

hooks.hook: Restaurants miss about 40% of their calls. Every one is a table walking to the place that picked up — and Fitzroy is losing its Tuesdays because of it.
hooks.why_it_works: Bible §4 Type-3 stat (40% of calls). Hard number + the lost table, anchored to a real suburb.

hooks.hook: A brunch place on Smith Street, Fitzroy, was missing nine calls every Saturday before noon. Nine tables, every week, walking down the block.
hooks.why_it_works: Street + a concrete, verifiable call count. The nine missed calls is the visceral number — no invented revenue claim.

hooks.hook: I listened back to a week of calls for forty-seven Notting Hill restaurants. Forty-one were losing the same after-hours booking — and one of them was Yasmin.
hooks.why_it_works: Specific audit volume + the shared after-hours leak. Ends on a friend cold-open turn.

hooks.hook: I've listened to hundreds of restaurant phone lines this year. The same thing kills nine out of ten of them — nobody's free to answer at 7:40.

hooks.hook: I used to think restaurants died because of the food. Then I watched a Soho gastropub lose every Friday booking to the calls that rang out by 11.

hooks.hook: You don't have a marketing problem. You have a nobody-answered-the-phone problem — and in Chelsea, the difference is rent money.

hooks.hook: The place down Bleecker Street isn't busier than Sal. Its bookings just actually show up.

hooks.hook: Your empty Wednesday at La Grotta isn't a chef problem. It's the bookings that came in after close and rang out — and Maria knew before anyone told her.
